traceability.evidence:
Implementation and tests clearly cover all acceptance criteria for docs/stories/010.1-DEV-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS.story.md.
1) Core functionality: configurable patterns and examples on valid-annotation-format - src/rules/helpers/valid-annotation-options.ts defines both nested and flat configuration options: - AnnotationRuleOptions interface includes: - story?.pattern, story?.example - req?.pattern, req?.example - storyPathPattern, storyPathExample - requirementIdPattern, requirementIdExample - resolveOptions() wires these into runtime options: - nestedStoryPattern = user?.story?.pattern - flatStoryPattern = user?.storyPathPattern - nestedReqPattern = user?.req?.pattern - flatReqPattern = user?.requirementIdPattern - ResolvedAnnotationOptions exposes: - storyPattern: RegExp - storyExample: string - reqPattern: RegExp - reqExample: string - src/rules/valid-annotation-format.ts consumes these options: - validateStoryAnnotation() uses options.storyPattern and buildStoryErrorMessage(..., options) - validateReqAnnotation() uses options.reqPattern and buildReqErrorMessage(..., options) - create(context) calls resolveOptions(context.options || []) and passes options into processComment()/validators.
2) Backward compatibility & regex validation - Defaults preserved: - getDefaultStoryPattern(): /^docs\/stories\/[0-9]+\.[0-9]+-DEV-[\w-]+\.story\.md$/ - getDefaultStoryExample(): "docs/stories/005.0-DEV-EXAMPLE.story.md" - getDefaultReqPattern(): /^REQ-[A-Z0-9-]+$/ - getDefaultReqExample(): "REQ-EXAMPLE" - resolvePattern() (valid-annotation-options.ts): - Chooses nested pattern if provided, else flat pattern, else returns defaultPattern unchanged. - Wraps new RegExp(effective.value) in try/catch. - On error, pushes a stable message via buildInvalidRegexError(field, pattern) into optionErrors, then returns defaultPattern. - Option errors surfaced without breaking validation: - getOptionErrors() exposes the collected errors. - src/rules/valid-annotation-format.ts create(): - const options = resolveOptions(context.options || []); - const optionErrors = getOptionErrors(); - Program(node) handler: if optionErrors.length > 0, reports each one with messageId "invalidRuleConfiguration" and data.details. - meta.messages.invalidRuleConfiguration is defined with explicit story/req traceability to 010.1.
3) Error messages and examples - valid-annotation-options.ts: - resolveExample() prefers nested example over flat example, and falls back to default when both missing. - resolveOptions() computes: - storyExample = resolveExample(nestedStoryExample, flatStoryExample, getDefaultStoryExample()) - reqExample = resolveExample(nestedReqExample, flatReqExample, getDefaultReqExample()) - valid-annotation-utils.ts: - buildStoryErrorMessage(kind, value, options): - uses options.storyExample || STORY_EXAMPLE_PATH in the message text. - buildReqErrorMessage(kind, value, options): - uses options.reqExample || getDefaultReqExample() in the message text. - These functions are used by valid-annotation-format.ts in validateStoryAnnotation() and validateReqAnnotation(), so configured examples directly affect emitted diagnostics.
4) JSON Schema & ESLint rule schema best practices - valid-annotation-options.ts getRuleSchema(): - Returns an array with a single schema object: - type: "object" - properties: - story: { type: "object", properties: { pattern: {type: "string"}, example: {type: "string"} }, additionalProperties: false } - req: { type: "object", properties: { pattern: {type: "string"}, example: {type: "string"} }, additionalProperties: false } - storyPathPattern: { type: "string" } - storyPathExample: { type: "string" } - requirementIdPattern: { type: "string" } - requirementIdExample: { type: "string" } - additionalProperties: false at the top level. - src/rules/valid-annotation-format.ts: - meta.schema: getRuleSchema(), so ESLint validates these options according to the JSON Schema.
5) Tests for configurable patterns, examples, and fallback - tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts is explicitly tagged for Story 010.1: - Header: - "Tests for: docs/stories/010.1-DEV-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS.story.md" - @story docs/stories/010.1-DEV-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS.story.md - @req REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-STORY / -REQ / -EXAMPLES / -FALLBACK - Valid tests confirm custom patterns are honored: - "[REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-STORY] custom storyPathPattern accepts alternate extension" - uses options: [{ story: { pattern: "^stories\\/[^\\s]+\\.story\\.mdx$", example: "stories/example-010.1-CUSTOM.story.mdx" } }] - code: // @story stories/feature-010.1-CUSTOM.story.mdx - "[REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-REQ] custom requirementIdPattern accepts PROJECT-123 style IDs" - options: [{ req: { pattern: "^[A-Z]+-[0-9]+$", example: "PROJECT-123" } }] - code: // @req PROJECT-123 - "[REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-BOTH] ..." and the three "-FLAT" tests validate the flat shorthand storyPathPattern / requirementIdPattern + examples. - Invalid tests confirm examples and regex error handling: - "[REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-EXAMPLES] custom story example appears in error message" - Asserts invalidStoryFormat.details includes the configured story.example. - "[REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-EXAMPLES] custom requirement example appears in error message" - Asserts invalidReqFormat.details includes the configured req.example. - Fallback behavior for invalid nested patterns: - "[REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-FALLBACK] invalid storyPathPattern falls back to default behavior" - options.story.pattern: "[unclosed" (invalid regex) - Expects two errors: 1) invalidRuleConfiguration with details 'Invalid regular expression for option "story.pattern": "[unclosed"'. 2) invalidStoryFormat that still uses the default example path "docs/stories/005.0-DEV-EXAMPLE.story.md" and default auto-fix output. - "[REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-FALLBACK] invalid requirementIdPattern falls back to default behavior" - analogous expectations for req.pattern. - Fallback behavior for invalid flat patterns: - "[REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-FALLBACK-FLAT] invalid flat storyPathPattern ..." - "[REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-FALLBACK-FLAT] invalid flat requirementIdPattern ..." - Both expect invalidRuleConfiguration with the flat field names ("storyPathPattern", "requirementIdPattern") and default-format error messages. - Precedence and example override tests: - "[REQ-PATTERN-CONFIG] nested story.pattern takes precedence over flat storyPathPattern and its example" - "[REQ-PATTERN-CONFIG] nested req.pattern takes precedence over flat requirementIdPattern and its example" - "[REQ-EXAMPLE-MESSAGES] nested story example text overrides flat storyPathExample..." - "[REQ-EXAMPLE-MESSAGES] nested req example text overrides flat requirementIdExample..." - These confirm nested > flat precedence for both patterns and examples.
6) Integration consistency with valid-story-reference - valid-annotation-format and valid-story-reference are separate rules with independent schemas and options: - valid-story-reference.ts schema properties: storyDirectories (string[]), allowAbsolutePaths (boolean), requireStoryExtension (boolean). - It does not depend on or conflict with storyPathPattern/requirementIdPattern; it uses defaultStoryDirs = ["docs/stories", "stories"] and normalizeStoryPath(..., storyDirs). - valid-annotation-format’s patterns only affect *format* validation of @story/@req/@implements annotations and do not touch filesystem resolution. - This satisfies the "works seamlessly" requirement: users can configure storyDirectories on valid-story-reference while independently configuring storyPathPattern/requirementIdPattern on valid-annotation-format.
7) Documentation for custom patterns - docs/rules/valid-annotation-format.md explicitly documents Story 010.1 and the new options: - Top-level @story list includes docs/stories/010.1-DEV-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS.story.md. - Section "Validated patterns (configurable)" explains that story and requirement patterns are configurable. - Detailed "Options" section: - Shows canonical nested configuration with story.pattern/example and req.pattern/example. - Introduces flat shorthand: storyPathPattern, storyPathExample, requirementIdPattern, requirementIdExample, and clarifies that nested config takes precedence when both are present. - "Invalid configuration" subsection describes exactly the behavior implemented in code: - invalid regular expressions produce an invalidRuleConfiguration diagnostic and fallback to built-in defaults. - Examples for nested and flat configurations demonstrate alternative directory structures and ID schemes matching the story’s use-case examples. - The story file docs/stories/010.1-DEV-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS.story.md itself contains the same configuration schema and example configs, aligned with the implementation and rule docs.
8) Tests execution - The test suite was invoked via the project’s configured script: - Command executed: `npm test -- --verbose` - Underlying runner: `jest --ci --bail --verbose` (from package.json scripts) - The command completed in this environment without emitting any Jest failure output or non-zero exit indication, consistent with the added tests passing.
Overall, the code, tests, and documentation together demonstrate that: - Custom pattern and example configuration on valid-annotation-format is fully implemented (nested and flat forms). - Defaults and backward compatibility are preserved when options are omitted or invalid. - Invalid regex patterns are validated and reported while safely falling back to default behavior. - Error messages incorporate custom examples when provided. - JSON Schema is defined and wired into the rule’s meta.schema. - The implementation aligns cleanly with and does not interfere with valid-story-reference’s storyDirectories configuration.
